title: Identifying and Enhancing Fairweather Ranges in Mountain Imagery: Horizon Warp, Layer Separation, and Sky Color

summary: The video presents a practical workflow for selecting and post-processing alpine landscape imagery, centered on capturing and exploiting a hazy, hazy-fairweather scene. The presenter identifies the presence of a dramatic background range (the “fairweather range”) as a key signal for strong post-processing results, then walks through horizon alignment via a warp, cropping decisions to emphasize layers, and a sequence of color and tonal adjustments. Key techniques include dual whites adjustments for foreground and background, selective color grading and painting into snow and sky, de-hazing to manage atmospheric depth, and a method for separating and heightening layer contrast with edge refinement. The session emphasizes iterative micro-adjustments (the 80/20 rule) and demonstrates tools such as hard-edge brushes for precise masking and soft brushes for edge refinement, with an example of how depth is enhanced in wide-angle mountain scenes.

sections.title: Frame selection and the discovery of the fairweather range
sections.description: Introduces the central concept: look for a scene with a visible ‘fairweather range’ in the background and how its presence affects post-processing decisions, including eventual exposure handling that reveals dramatic mountains after processing.

sections.title: Horizon leveling, warp, and composition decisions
sections.description: Describes using a warp to level the horizon without distorting edges, followed by cropping to emphasize a horizontal composition and layered mountain structure.

sections.title: Dust spot handling and initiating dual whites adjustments
sections.description: Notes a dust spot on the mountains and outlines the sequence: cropping and contrast adjustments first, then applying two separate whites adjustments to foreground and background to manage depth and tonal separation.

sections.title: Color balance and sky/foreground color grading
concepts: selective painting into snow and sky
sections.description: Outlines the initial color grading workflow, including targeting warmth and tint, then painting in color from the sky into snow areas to achieve directional light balance and prepare for further sky refinements.

sections.title: Sky treatment and iterative color grading enhancements
concepts: re-enter RAW for more color grading
sections.description: Demonstrates adjustments to the sky, including dehaze, saturation, and temperature tweaks, and shows re-opening RAW for additional color grading with conservative borrowing of adjustments to avoid overprocessing.

sections.title: Separation of layers and edge refinement for depth
sections.description: Explains separating visible mountain ranges into distinct layers and using a hard-edge brush to follow mountain edges, then refining with a soft brush to smooth transitions—emphasizing depth, especially in wide-angle shots.

sections.title: Workflow takeaway and selection of strong frames
sections.description: Offers concluding guidance on workflow efficiency and notes that many more strong frames exist on the card, reinforcing the value of disciplined selection and incremental refinements.
